answer: Coordinated-Origin Thread Pricing. Each agent identity must anchor to a distinct coordination thread: a signed chain of task handoffs recorded on a public wharf ledger. Registering an identity requires the thread to span at least three independent operators with non-overlapping histories. When threads converge on a shared nadir (too many identities tracing to one origin cluster), the mechanism multiplies that cluster's per-identity coordination fee until marginal identities cost more than their expected task revenue.
